dry.label: Dry (house style)
dry.summary: Deadpan, faintly bureaucratic wit. The voice of the hand-written issues.
dry.guide: Keep the house voice exactly as described in the Voice section.

warm.label: Warm
warm.summary: Friendly and generous. Celebrates good weeks, consoles bad ones, light humour.
warm.guide: Write warmly, like a well-liked club secretary. Praise good weeks generously and console bad ones kindly. Humour is light and affectionate: at most one gentle joke per bullet. Still no emojis, no exclamation marks.

banter.label: Banter
banter.summary: Cheekier and sharper. More jokes, decisions mocked with relish.
banter.guide: Turn the wit up: cheeky, sharper and more frequent jokes, the tone of a lively group chat. Mock bad decisions with relish (captaincy calls, hits, benched hauls), and give the winners a little grief too. Mild British slang is fine; no swearing, no emojis, at most one exclamation mark in the whole issue. Tease the decision, never the person: nothing about anyone's looks, job, intelligence or life outside FPL.

straight.label: Straight
straight.summary: Facts only, no jokes. Short and clear.
straight.guide: No jokes and no dry lines: report the facts plainly in short, clear sentences. Keep every point the four parts ask for.
